npx wasm-html-to-image <input> [options]

Option Flag Default Description --output <path> -o Input based Target output path --width <number> -w 800 Viewport width --height <number> -h auto Viewport height --format <format> -f png Format (svg, png, pdf, jpeg, webp, apng, gif, tiff, avif, jxl, raw, thumbhash) --scale <n> - 1 Pixel density of raster output from HTML (e.g. 3.125 draws an 800px layout as 2500px) --dpi <n> - 96 × scale Resolution written to tiff, in pixels per inch --color-space <srgb|cmyk> - srgb Output color space of tiff / pdf. cmyk is for print (device conversion, no ICC profile) --quality <number> -q 85 Encode quality 0–100 --base-url <url> - From input Base URL for relative resources; defaults to the post-redirect URL (URL input) or the file's directory, explicit wins --animation <duration-ms> - Disabled Sample the document's opacity / transform / color / background-color @keyframes into an animated WebP / APNG / GIF (one loop length in ms; webp, apng and gif output only; clamped to 5000 ms) --animation-fps <n> - 15 Animation sampling fps (used with --animation; ~75 frames total cap) --animation-loop <n> - 0 (infinite) How many times the animated WebP / APNG / GIF repeats (0 = infinite, 1 = play once; used with --animation) --markdown - Auto-detect Treat input as Markdown (implied by .md / .markdown file extension) --template <name|file> - default Document template (default, report, proposal, book, paper, compact, or path to .json / .css) --list-templates - - List available bundled templates and exit --page-size <size> - From template Page size (A3, A4, A5, B4, B5, Letter, or two lengths like "210mm 297mm") --accent <color> - From template Accent color for headings, links, and cover elements (e.g. "#c2410c") --body-font <family> - From template Body font family name --stamp <text> - None Text stamped into the running header of every page (e.g. DRAFT, Confidential) --cover / --no-cover - From template Force enable / disable the cover page --no-toc - - Disable the table of contents page (enabled by default for PDF output) --toc-depth <n> - 3 Deepest heading level included in the table of contents (1–6) --no-outline - - Disable PDF bookmarks / outline generation (enabled by default) --no-math - - Disable KaTeX math typesetting (enabled by default when katex is installed) --markdown-theme <light|dark> - light Theme for the built-in Markdown stylesheet --markdown-css <path> - None Path to extra stylesheet appended after the built-in styles --mermaid - automatic for .mmd / .mermaid Treat the input as a Mermaid diagram (needed for inline text and stdin) --mermaid-theme <name> - light Colour theme of the diagram (light, dark, neutral, forest, nord, dracula, solarized-light, solarized-dark, rose-pine, sepia) --mermaid-mode <mode> - strict How much a broken source is forgiven: strict, compat, recover --mermaid-directives - off Honour %%{init}%% and frontmatter config: in the source

# Render local HTML to WebP npx wasm-html-to-image template.html -o card.webp -w 1200 -h 630 -f webp -q 90 # Capture screenshot from URL npx wasm-html-to-image https://example.com -o site.png -w 1280 -h 720 # Render Markdown to a PDF document (with TOC and bookmarks) npx wasm-html-to-image report.md -o report.pdf # Render Markdown with report template, custom accent, and DRAFT stamp npx wasm-html-to-image report.md -o report.pdf --template report --accent "#c2410c" --stamp DRAFT # Render Markdown with book template in A5 size without TOC npx wasm-html-to-image book.md -o book.pdf --template book --page-size A5 --no-toc # List available document templates npx wasm-html-to-image --list-templates # Turn an opacity / transform / color @keyframes animation into an animated WebP npx wasm-html-to-image loader.html -o loader.webp -f webp --animation 2000 --animation-fps 20 # Play the animated WebP once instead of looping forever npx wasm-html-to-image loader.html -o loader.webp -f webp --animation 2000 --animation-loop 1

wasm-html-to-image/markdown converts GitHub-flavoured Markdown (GFM) into beautifully styled HTML pages and multi-page PDF documents. It is implemented in pure JavaScript with no Node.js platform dependencies, running seamlessly across Node.js, modern browsers, and edge runtimes like Cloudflare Workers.

markdownToDocument() & markdownToHtml(): Produce HTML and complete PDF render options (headers, footers, metadata). Template System: 11 built-in templates (default, report, proposal, book, paper, compact, manual, minutes, letter, slides, invoice) for ready-to-use professional styling without writing CSS. Automatic Table of Contents (TOC): Generates a table of contents with exact destination page numbers filled in during PDF pagination. Automatic PDF Bookmarks (Outline): Creates nested PDF document outlines from h1–h6 headings. Smart Page Break Handling: Avoids orphan headings (break-after: avoid) and prevents breaking code blocks and tables across page boundaries. YAML Front Matter: Parses document metadata (title, subtitle, author, date, template, stamp, cover, accent, etc.). Syntax Highlighting: Built-in highlight.js covering 20+ programming languages. Mermaid diagrams: ```mermaid blocks (flowchart, sequence, state, class, ER, bar/line chart) are drawn inside the engine. KaTeX Mathematical Typesetting (/markdown-math): High-accuracy rendering for inline $…$ and display $$…$$ equations.

Use markdownToDocument() to retrieve both the document HTML and the required PDF options (such as running headers and footers), then pass them to render(): import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image"; import { markdownToDocument } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; const md = `--- title: Quarterly Performance Report subtitle: Q3 2026 author: Taro Yamada date: 2026-10-29 template: report accent: "#2563eb" stamp: CONFIDENTIAL --- # Executive Summary Revenue increased by **+15.2%** year-over-year. # Key Performance Indicators | KPI | Target | Actual | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Gross Margin | $5.0M | $5.4M | | New Customers | 120 | 135 | `; // Retrieve HTML and PDF layout options const { html, renderOptions } = markdownToDocument(md, { paged: true, // Enable page margins and pagination optimization }); const { data } = await render({ value: html, format: "pdf", ...renderOptions, }); await fs.writeFile("report.pdf", Buffer.from(data));

Use markdownToHtml() when rendering standalone images: import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image"; import { markdownToHtml } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; const html = markdownToHtml("# Document Title\n\nContent...", { theme: "dark", maxWidth: 800, }); const { data } = await render({ value: html, width: 900, format: "png", });

documents.t: Templates configure the document's typography, page size, margins, running headers/footers, and cover/contents pages. All templates support both light and dark themes. Template Intended Use Layout & Features default Web images, quick PDFs Clean GitHub-like style report Business reports, specs A4, cover page, table of contents, accent colour, title in header, author and n / N in footer proposal Proposals, quotations A4, cover, accent bars on sections, tinted table headers, call-out quotes, title and n / N in the footer book Books, long-form reading A5, serif, justified text, each chapter (h1) starts on a new page, cover, TOC, page numbers paper Technical papers, essays A4, serif, justified text, tight line-height, page number in footer compact Notes, cheat sheets 12px font, 12mm margins, no cover or TOC manual Manuals, specifications A4, cover, contents, numbered headings, each chapter (h1) on a new page, call-outs, title in the header and page number in the footer minutes Meeting minutes A4, no cover or contents, ruled title, tinted table headers, title and date in the header letter Letters, notices A4, serif, wide margins, generous leading, .right and .center classes for the address block and date slides Presentations A4 landscape, 28px text, each h2 on its own page, --- ignored, with a cover invoice Invoices, quotations A4, large right-aligned title, accent table header, emphasised last row, call-out box for notes Inspect available templates with listTemplates(): import { listTemplates } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; console.log(listTemplates());

Place front matter at the top of the file enclosed by ---: --- title: System Architecture Spec
v2.0 subtitle: Next-generation Graphics Pipeline author: Core Engineering Team date: 2026-10-29 template: report accent: "#059669" font: sans-serif page_size: A4 stamp: DRAFT cover: true toc: true logo: https://example.com/logo.png lang: en ---
Settings are resolved in the following order: Template defaults (template.defaults) Front matter attributes API options (options.settings, options.title, etc.)

These front matter keys also change the page: Key Value Effect header / footer HTML Running header and footer (replacing the template's). {{title}}, {{author}}, {{date}}, {{stamp}}, {{pageNumber}}, {{totalPages}} and {{chapter}} (the h1 the page shows first, else the chapter before it) work. The book header shows the chapter margin 20mm 18mm Page margin (a CSS margin value) orientation landscape Turn the paper sideways toc_depth 1 to 6 Deepest heading level in the contents toc_title text Heading of the contents page (Contents) cover_style band / plain / center Look of the cover numbering true Number the headings 1, 1.1, 1.1.1 footnotes end Where footnotes go: end lists them after the text, page sets each at the foot of the page that refers to it (PDF; if one note is taller than a third of a page, the list stays at the end) mermaid_theme a name (nord, ...) Draw the diagrams with a named theme instead of the document's light / dark colours (pick one that suits the page: dracula, nord or dark on a dark document) mermaid_mode compat / recover How much a broken diagram is forgiven mermaid_directives true Honour %%{init}%% and frontmatter inside the diagrams With a template that has a cover, the cover carries no header or footer (page numbers still count it as page 1).

Call-outs: a block quote that starts with [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION] becomes a coloured box (the title is Japanese with lang: ja). Numbered figures: an image with a title, ![alt](src "Title"), becomes a figure captioned Figure 1 Title. Page break: <!-- pagebreak --> forces a new page. Footnotes: [^name] in the text and [^name]: the note anywhere put a list of notes at the end, numbered by first use. Tables span the text width in report, proposal, book and paper. Long code lines wrap at the right edge instead of being cut.

When paged: true (or CLI PDF output) is specified: Contents Page: Headings down to level 3 (by default) are indexed. Page numbers are dynamically linked to the layout output. Bookmarks (Outline): Headings h1–h6 automatically form the PDF reader outline tree. In-page Links: Links such as [details](#setup) work seamlessly inside the PDF. // Customise depth and heading const { html, renderOptions } = markdownToDocument(md, { paged: true, toc: { depth: 2, title: "Contents" }, }); // Disable TOC page const { html, renderOptions } = markdownToDocument(md, { paged: true, toc: false, }); // Disable PDF bookmarks await render({ value: html, format: "pdf", pdfOutline: false, ...renderOptions, });

A ```mermaid code block is drawn by the engine itself as vector graphics: no browser or extra library, and in a PDF the text stays selectable. ```mermaid graph LR A[Order] --> B{In stock?} B -->|yes| C[Ship] B -->|no| D[Reorder] ``` Diagram Starts with Flowchart graph / flowchart Sequence sequenceDiagram State stateDiagram-v2 Class classDiagram ER erDiagram Bar / line chart xychart-beta Pie chart pie Gantt chart gantt Mind map mindmap Timeline timeline User journey journey Quadrant chart quadrantChart Git graph gitGraph Kanban kanban Packet packet-beta Sankey sankey-beta Requirement requirementDiagram Block block-beta (nested blocks are not supported) C4 C4Context / C4Container / C4Component / C4Dynamic / C4Deployment Architecture architecture-beta Venn venn-beta Ishikawa (fishbone) ishikawa-beta Tree view treeView-beta Treemap treemap-beta Radar radar-beta Version banner info Colours follow the theme (light / dark). A diagram is never split across pages. accTitle: Title and accDescr: Description (accDescr { ... } for several lines) are not drawn; they become the SVG <title> and <desc>, which screen readers announce. Pass mermaid: false to show them as plain code blocks. An unsupported type (architecture-beta, C4, zenuml, ...) or a syntax error shows an error box where the diagram would be.
renderMermaid() (a diagram alone as an SVG string or an image), themes, input repair and CSS control are described in Mermaid Conversion.

documents.t: Pass katexMath() from wasm-html-to-image/markdown-math to render inline $…$ and display $$…$$ TeX equations: import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image"; import { markdownToHtml } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; import { katexMath } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown-math"; const md = ` Euler's identity: $e^{i\\pi} + 1 = 0$ Quadratic formula: $$ x = \\frac{-b \\pm \\sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} $$ `; const html = markdownToHtml(md, { math: katexMath(), // Use { fontBase: "https://your-host/fonts" } to self-host KaTeX fonts });

Define your own template using a JavaScript object or JSON file: const myTemplate = { type: { font: "serif", size: 14, lineHeight: 1.7, justify: true, chapterBreak: true, }, page: { size: "B5", margin: "18mm", footer: `
{{pageNumber}} / {{totalPages}}
`, }, defaults: { cover: true, toc: true, accent: "#0f766e", }, }; const doc = markdownToDocument(md, { template: myTemplate, paged: true });

Put the name of a bundled template in extends and override its type, page and defaults field by field; your css is appended after the base's. defineTemplate() only type-checks and returns the value unchanged. import { defineTemplate, markdownToDocument } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; const mine = defineTemplate({ extends: "report", type: { size: 13 }, defaults: { accent: "#0f766e" }, css: ".markdown-body h2 { border-bottom-style: dashed; }", }); const doc = markdownToDocument(md, { template: mine, paged: true }); From the CLI, a JSON file such as { "extends": "report", "defaults": { "accent": "#0f766e" } } works with --template mine.json.
In a template's css, use var(--surface), var(--border), var(--muted), var(--text) and var(--accent) instead of fixed colours, so the template follows both the light and the dark theme.

The engine draws Mermaid diagrams itself, as vectors. No browser, Puppeteer or Mermaid JavaScript is needed. There are three ways to use it. Way Entry Good for A ```mermaid fence in Markdown wasm-html-to-image/markdown Diagrams inside a document; they go into the PDF as they are <pre class="mermaid"> / <div class="mermaid"> in HTML render() A diagram inside an HTML page The diagram alone renderMermaid() An SVG string or a PNG (or other image) of one diagram All three use the same engine and the same diagram types. Text is measured with the real fonts, so Japanese labels fit exactly.

```mermaid graph LR A[Order] --> B{In stock?} B -->|yes| C[Ship] B -->|no| D[Reorder] ``` In a PDF a diagram is never split across pages, and its text stays selectable vector text. Pass mermaid: false to show it as an ordinary code block. See Markdown Conversion for more.

sequenceDiagram A->>B: Hello 
 works the same. The element's text is the diagram source. Colours come from the page's CSS (CSS control).

Give a .mmd / .mermaid file and the output is an image (or SVG, or PDF) sized to the diagram; the extension of -o picks the format. npx wasm-html-to-image flow.mmd -o flow.svg npx wasm-html-to-image flow.mmd -o flow.png --mermaid-theme nord npx wasm-html-to-image "graph LR; A-->B" --mermaid -o ab.png # inline text cat flow.mmd | npx wasm-html-to-image - --mermaid -o flow.webp --mermaid-mode recover The image width is fixed only when you pass -w. --accent sets the arrow colour and --mermaid-directives honours %%{init}%% in the source.

import { renderMermaid } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const { data: svg } = await renderMermaid("graph LR\n A --> B"); // an SVG string const { data: png } = await renderMermaid("graph LR\n A --> B", { format: "png", theme: "dark", }); The output is sized to the diagram (plus the padding). data is a string for format: "svg" and a Uint8Array for everything else. Entry renderMermaid wasm-html-to-image/single (and wasm-html-to-image on Node.js and similar) Yes wasm-html-to-image/workers Yes (drawn on the worker pool) /workerd, /edge-light (on Cloudflare Workers wasm-html-to-image resolves here too) No renderMermaid; use renderMermaidWith((options) => render(options, wasm), source, options) mermaidToHtml(source, options) returns an HTML string with one diagram, for when you want a page.

Option Default Description format "svg" svg, png, webp, jpeg, avif, jxl, pdf, ... theme "light" Colour scheme (see Themes); a key of MERMAID_THEMES accent the theme's Colour of arrows and bars (any CSS colour) padding 16 Space around the diagram, px width diagram width + padding Image width, px background transparent for SVG, the theme's background for images Page background (a CSS colour or "transparent") mode "strict" How much a broken source is forgiven (see Input repair) directives false Honour %%{init: {...}}%% and frontmatter config: written in the source maxLines 2000 Most lines of text a diagram may have (comments and blank lines are free). 0 lifts the limit maxSourceBytes 200000 Largest diagram source in bytes. 0 lifts the limit onWarning none (warning) => void: gets MERMAID_ERROR when the diagram did not parse, and one MERMAID_RECOVERED for each change the input repair made

A <div class="mermaid"> or a Markdown diagram takes its colours and behaviour from CSS custom properties on the element or an ancestor. Property Meaning color Text colour (when there is no --mermaid-fg) --mermaid-theme A named theme (for example nord). The single colours below are applied on top of it --mermaid-fg / --mermaid-bg Text and background colour. Every other colour is derived from these two --mermaid-accent Colour of arrows and bars --mermaid-line Colour of lines --mermaid-muted Secondary text (edge labels, ...) --mermaid-surface Node fill --mermaid-border Node outline --mermaid-mode compat or recover --mermaid-directives on honours %%{init}%% and frontmatter <style> .mermaid { --mermaid-theme: dracula; --mermaid-accent: #ff79c6; } </style>

Name Text Background Note light (default) #1f2328 #ffffff dark #e6edf3 #0d1117 neutral #222222 #ffffff Mostly grey forest #1b3a2a #ffffff Green accent nord #eceff4 #2e3440 dracula #f8f8f2 #282a36 solarized-light #586e75 #fdf6e3 solarized-dark #93a1a1 #002b36 rose-pine #e0def4 #191724 sepia #433422 #f4ecd8 The same names work in %%{init: {"theme": "dark"}}%% (default and base mean light). themeVariables keys primaryColor, primaryBorderColor, lineColor, textColor, background and secondaryTextColor are applied on top of the theme. Directives only take effect with directives: true (or --mermaid-directives: on): the page that places a diagram decides its colours, not the author of the diagram.

mode chooses how much a broken source is forgiven. Mode Forgives strict (default) Nothing. A mistake shows as an error box. A near-miss diagram keyword gets a hint: did you mean 'flowchart'? compat A keyword in the wrong case, a leading BOM, CRLF, and unfinished end / } blocks (up to 3) recover Everything in compat, plus a misspelt keyword (1 to 2 edits, when one keyword fits) and lines the diagram cannot read (skipped) What was repaired comes to onWarning, one MERMAID_RECOVERED at a time; a diagram that could not be read arrives as MERMAID_ERROR. await renderMermaid("flowchrt LR\n A --> B", { mode: "recover", onWarning: (w) => console.warn(w.code, w.message), // MERMAID_RECOVERED: `flowchrt` read as `flowchart` }); The CLI prints the same on stderr. When a diagram cannot be read it still writes the image with the error box, and then exits with status 1, so a script or CI notices.

Diagram Starts with Flowchart graph / flowchart Sequence sequenceDiagram State stateDiagram-v2 Class classDiagram ER erDiagram Requirement requirementDiagram Block block-beta (block:id ... end groups nest) C4 C4Context / C4Container / C4Component / C4Dynamic / C4Deployment Architecture architecture-beta Gantt gantt Pie pie Bar / line chart xychart-beta Quadrant quadrantChart Radar radar-beta Sankey sankey-beta Treemap treemap-beta Venn venn-beta Mind map mindmap Timeline timeline User journey journey Git graph gitGraph Kanban kanban Packet packet-beta Ishikawa (fishbone) ishikawa-beta Tree view treeView-beta Version banner info An unsupported type (zenuml, wardley-beta, eventmodeling, ...) shows as an error box where the diagram would be. note The syntax of the -beta diagrams changes often in Mermaid itself. venn-beta, ishikawa-beta, treeView-beta, treemap-beta, radar-beta and architecture-beta may differ from the latest Mermaid in details. If you find a difference, use recover mode to see which lines were skipped, and open an issue.

Styling: classDef, class, ::: and style work in flowcharts, state, class (with cssClass), ER and block diagrams. linkStyle is flowcharts only. Accessibility: accTitle: Title and accDescr: Description (accDescr { ... } for several lines) are not drawn; they become the SVG <title> and <desc>. Frontmatter: a leading --- block is skipped. With directives on, its config: (theme, themeVariables) is applied. Comments: lines starting with %% are ignored.

The layout of a big graph grows faster than its size (measured: a flowchart takes seconds at 600 nodes and minutes at 1500). So that a server that draws whatever a user sends cannot be stalled by one huge diagram, there are limits on lines (default 2000) and on source size (default 200000 bytes). A diagram over either becomes an error box (MERMAID_ERROR). Change them with maxLines / maxSourceBytes (in CSS: --mermaid-max-lines / --mermaid-max-bytes).

A syntax error or an unsupported diagram shows as a one-line error box (Mermaid: ...) where the diagram would be; the rest of the document still converts. renderMermaid() returns an SVG of the same box.

The playground's "Mermaid" tab switches the sample (one per diagram type, 26 in all), theme, input repair, output format (SVG / PNG / WebP / JPEG / AVIF / JXL / PDF), accent colour and directives on the spot. "Gallery" draws every sample with the current settings. The settings live in the URL, and so does the diagram itself (compressed, up to about 6000 characters, as src=), so one link shares the diagram and how it is drawn (for example ?mode=mermaid&theme=nord&format=png&view=gallery).
render() is the primary function for converting HTML or raw images into the target format.

Ignored for svg / pdf and for image input. dpi number 96 × scale Resolution written to tiff, in pixels per inch. A print shop reads the physical size from it. colorSpace "srgb" | "cmyk" "srgb" Output color space of tiff and pdf. "cmyk" is for print: TIFF becomes a separated CMYK image with transparency flattened onto white, and PDF has every fill, stroke and image rewritten to DeviceCMYK. The conversion is the plain device formula (K = 1 − max(R,G,B), black stays K only) with no ICC profile, so saturated screen colors are not gamut-mapped. Ignored for other formats.

wasm-html-to-image merges an HTML layout/rendering pipeline and an image optimization/encoding pipeline into a single native WebAssembly binary. Traditional setups require two separate libraries: one rendering HTML to PNG, and another re-encoding PNG to WebP or AVIF. This causes substantial memory allocations and data copying across JavaScript boundaries. wasm-html-to-image eliminates this overhead by piping the rendered Bitmap directly to the encoder within the single Skia-WASM module.

Resource Discovery (satoru_collect_resources): Parses image URLs, @font-face rules, and CSS backgrounds from HTML/CSS. Resource Injection (satoru_add_resource): TypeScript fetches needed resources concurrently using in-memory process caches. Layout & Painting: litehtml computes the box layout, HarfBuzz/SkUnicode shapes text, and Skia renders to an off-screen surface. Output Generation: svg / pdf: Skia streams vector commands directly. Raster formats: Rendered Bitmap is piped straight to native encoders without leaving WASM linear memory.

When given image buffers or data URLs: Direct Decoding: Bypasses the HTML layout engine completely. Transformations: Applies width, height, fit, and crop directly in the image pipeline. Encoding: Compresses to WebP, AVIF, JXL, JPEG, RAW pixels, or ThumbHash.

Richer images stay RGBA. webp, apng and gif produce an animated image when (apng without animation is a plain PNG; gif uses a 256-color dithered palette and composites transparency over white) animation: { duration, fps, loop } (CLI: --animation) is set. opacity, transform (translate / rotate / scale only) and color / background-color @keyframes are sampled; the default is 15 fps with caps of 5 s (duration is clamped to 5000 ms) / ~75 frames. The repeat count is set with loop (CLI: --animation-loop) and defaults to 0 (infinite).

Box Model: Margins, paddings, borders, box-sizing (border-box, content-box), aspect-ratio, and logical properties (margin-inline, padding-block, etc.). Flexbox: Multi-pass resolution conforming to W3C Flexbox specs (flex-direction, justify-content, align-items, flex-wrap, gap, row-gap, column-gap, etc.). Block & Table Layout: overflow: clip (clips like hidden; overflow-clip-margin is not supported), display: flow-root (contains floats, stops margin collapsing), explicit display: table-header-group / table-footer-group (placed first / last, repeated in PDF pagination like ), table-caption, and / backgrounds. Text Truncation & Stroke: max-lines (standard -webkit-line-clamp, implies overflow: hidden), block-ellipsis: auto | no-ellipsis | "", text-fit: grow | shrink [%] (rescales the font so the widest line fits; up to 3 relayout passes), and stroke-linejoin for -webkit-text-stroke (miter-clip / arcs fall back to miter). Line Breaking, Alignment & Hyphenation: line-break (CJK kinsoku strength: strict keeps small kana and ー off the line start, loose lets a line start with iteration marks, anywhere breaks anywhere), text-align-last (including justify), text-justify (none stops justification, inter-word stretches spaces only, inter-character / distribute also stretch between characters), tab-size (number of spaces or a length; tab stops measured from the line start), hyphens (-webkit-hyphens alias) and hyphenate-character. A soft hyphen (­) shows a hyphen only when the line breaks there; hyphens: auto splits English words (lang="en*") with a heuristic, there is no dictionary. The auto hyphen is -. Non-standard properties: flex-line-count (a takumi extension) is not adopted: it is not part of any CSS specification and is ignored (the number of flex lines follows from the content and the container width). Grid Layout: Grid tracks (grid-template-columns/rows, the grid-template / grid shorthands), item placement (grid-column/row), implicit tracks (grid-auto-columns/rows), grid-auto-flow (row, column, and dense hole filling), place-items, gap. Typography & Internationalization: HarfBuzz text shaping, bidirectional text (BiDi), unicode-bidi (bidi-override / isolate-override map to line-item order; embed / isolate boundaries and per-run glyph reversal are partial), line-breaking for CJK, Latin, Arabic, and Emoji. Vertical text (writing-mode: vertical-rl), multi-line truncation (-webkit-line-clamp / max-lines + block-ellipsis / text-overflow: ellipsis), text-transform, and text stroke (-webkit-text-stroke). Fonts for scripts missing from Noto Sans JP (Hangul, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai, Devanagari, Greek) and for color emoji are fetched on demand from external CDNs (Google Fonts / jsDelivr) only when such characters appear. Font Features: font-feature-settings, font-variant-* (-ligatures, -numeric, -east-asian, -caps, -position), font-kerning, font-variation-settings, font-stretch, font-optical-sizing (auto drives the opsz axis from the font size, none keeps the default, an explicit opsz in font-variation-settings always wins), font-synthesis (+ longhands; none disables synthetic bold / italic, the synthetic small-caps / sub-super variants do not exist in the engine). OpenType features (palt, kern, liga, pnum, zero, …) are applied through HarfBuzz per element; variable axes (wght, wdth, …) and stretch keywords/percentages are supported. Synthetic small-caps, synthetic sub/super, @font-face stretch descriptors, and optical sizing are partial or unsupported. Text Decoration: text-decoration (-line, -style, -color, -thickness), text-decoration-skip-ink, text-underline-position, text-underline-offset. Solid, dashed, dotted, double, and wavy underlines, overlines, and line-throughs; skip-ink splits the line around glyph ink and also applies to vertical writing. Percentages for thickness and underline-offset resolve against the element's font size. Visual Effects: Box shadows (multiple shadows, inset), border-radii (elliptical, individual corners), box-decoration-break: clone (PDF page fragments of block boxes get complete borders, corners and background; inline line breaks are unaffected), corner-shape (round / scoop / bevel / notch / squircle / square / superellipse() plus per-corner longhands; applied to backgrounds, borders, box-shadow and clipping), transforms, opacity, filters (blur, drop-shadow), backdrop filters, blend modes (mix-blend-mode, background-blend-mode), and image-rendering (pixelated uses nearest-neighbour sampling for and background images, including tiles; crisp-edges is unsupported). Motion Path: offset-path (ray(), path(), basic shapes), offset-distance, offset-rotate, offset-anchor, offset-position, and the offset shorthand. Position and tangent rotation along the path are supported with Chromium-checked grammar (lengths including calc(), coordinate boxes). url() references and strict handling are unsupported. Clipping & Shapes: Native Skia vector clipping paths (circle(), ellipse(), polygon(), path(), inset(), with clip-rule: evenodd), and alpha masks (mask, mask-image, mask-size, mask-repeat, mask-position; images and gradients, tiled). Inline SVG: Direct embedded

wasm-html-to-image is a lightweight static renderer based on litehtml and Skia, not a headless browser. Keep the following constraints in mind when writing templates: NO JavaScript: <script> tags, DOM event listeners, and DOM APIs do not run. Partial CSS Animation Support: transition is not evaluated. @keyframes are ignored by default (only static styles paint), but passing animation: { duration, fps, loop } (CLI: --animation) samples opacity, transform and color / background-color @keyframes into an animated WebP / APNG / GIF. The repeat count is set with loop (CLI: --animation-loop, default 0 = infinite). Defaults are 15 fps with caps of 5 s (duration is clamped to 5000 ms) / ~75 frames. The CSS animation-duration (including the animation shorthand, var() supported) is the length of one iteration; together with animation-delay and animation-iteration-count (a number or infinite) it defines the sampled timeline (infinite samples one iteration, alternate / alternate-reverse two). The API duration is an upper bound on the whole timeline and the API fps caps the frame rate. transform supports translate / rotate / scale only; when the function list differs between the keyframes the element keeps its static transform. An animation-timing-function inside a keyframe block applies to the interval that starts at that stop, and the element-level one (<style> or inline) is the default (linear / ease / ease-in / ease-out / ease-in-out / cubic-bezier() / steps() / step-start / step-end; applied to opacity, color and transform interpolation). animation-direction (normal / reverse / alternate / alternate-reverse) and animation-fill-mode (none / forwards / backwards / both) are honoured, so the value during animation-delay (backwards) and after the animation (forwards) is resolved; a negative animation-delay starts inside the first iteration. Every @keyframes block of the document animates all the elements its rule selects (several allowed); several animations on one element (animation: a 2s, b 3s or animation-name: a, b) are layered, the later one winning on shared properties; translateX / translateY are supported too. NO Canvas Scripting: <canvas> element 2D/WebGL contexts do not execute. Use inline <svg> or CSS shapes instead. NO Interactive States: :hover, :active, and :focus states do not trigger. NO Browser Web Storage: window, document, localStorage, and IndexedDB are unavailable.

Node.js (>=20): Full support across single, multi-threaded worker pools, and explicit modules. Cloudflare Workers: Full support via wasm-html-to-image/workerd. Vercel Edge Runtime: Full support via wasm-html-to-image/edge-light. Browsers: Runs client-side or within Web Workers. Deno & Bun: Fully compatible.

wasm-html-to-image is an ultra-fast, self-contained HTML-to-image and image conversion engine that consolidates an HTML rendering engine (Satoru) and an image optimization engine (wasm-image-optimization) into a single WebAssembly (Emscripten) module. It requires no heavy headless browsers like Chromium, Puppeteer, or Playwright, and runs portably across server-side runtimes, edge environments such as Cloudflare Workers, browsers, and the CLI.

Single Unified WASM Module: Parses HTML, calculates CSS layout, renders with Skia, and encodes images (WebP/AVIF/JPEG, etc.) inside one binary without passing intermediate frame buffers across JS boundaries. Versatile Inputs: Supports HTML strings, HTML string arrays (for multi-page PDF), Markdown, URLs, and raw image buffers (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, AVIF, BMP, Data URLs). Multiple Output Formats: Direct SVG vector output, high-quality PNG, JPEG, WebP, AVIF, raw pixels, ThumbHash, and multi-page PDF generation. Zero-Config render(): Import directly from wasm-html-to-image and render immediately without manual WASM loading or setup (automatically resolves workerd in Cloudflare Workers). Edge & Cloudflare Workers Ready: Along with auto-detection, dedicated wasm-html-to-image/workerd and edge-light subpaths fit constrained serverless edge environments. Parallel Worker Pool: Built-in multi-threaded pool in wasm-html-to-image/workers allows batch generation without stalling the main event loop. Rich Ecosystem Integration: Seamless JSX rendering for React and Preact, UnoCSS-based Tailwind CSS utility classes, and Markdown to image / beautiful PDF documents (templates, automatic TOC, bookmarks, and KaTeX math).

wasm-html-to-image functions not only as an HTML renderer but also as a high-performance native engine for image format conversion, resizing, compression, and ThumbHash generation. You can handle common image transformation tasks without pulling in heavy native dependencies like Sharp or ImageMagick.

Input image buffers (Uint8Array or Buffer) are automatically detected via magic bytes: Input Format (Auto-detected) Available Output Formats PNG webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf JPEG webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf WebP avif, jxl, webp, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf GIF (including animated) webp (with animation), png, jpeg, avif, jxl, etc. AVIF webp, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf BMP webp, avif, jxl, jpeg, png, raw, thumbhash, svg, pdf

import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const inputImage = await fs.readFile("photo.jpg"); // Convert JPEG -> WebP (quality: 80) const webp = await render({ value: inputImage, width: 800, format: "webp", quality: 80, fit: "contain", }); await fs.writeFile("photo.webp", Buffer.from(webp)); // Convert JPEG -> AVIF (highest compression) const avif = await render({ value: inputImage, width: 800, format: "avif", quality: 75, speed: 6, // 0 (slowest, best quality) to 10 (fastest) }); await fs.writeFile("photo.avif", Buffer.from(avif));

Dynamically serve images directly from Next.js App Router handlers (app/api/og/route.ts). // app/api/og/route.ts import { NextRequest } from "next/server"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; export async function GET(req: NextRequest) { const { searchParams } = new URL(req.url); const title = searchParams.get("title") || "Next.js Blog"; const png = await render({ value: `

${title}

`, width: 1200, height: 630, format: "png", }); return new Response(png, { headers: { "Content-Type": "image/png", "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=31536000, immutable", }, }); }

Building an automated Open Graph Image generator with custom HTML/CSS layouts. import { Hono } from "hono"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const app = new Hono(); app.get("/ogp", async (c) => { const title = c.req.query("title") || "No Title"; const html = `

${title}

`; const image = await render({ value: html, width: 1200, height: 630, format: "png", }); return new Response(image, { headers: { "Content-Type": "image/png", "Cache-Control": "public, max-age=86400", }, }); }); export default app;

Generate multi-page vector PDF documents by supplying an array of HTML strings (string[]). import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/single"; const pages = [ `

Monthly Summary

Page 1 Overview

`, `

Detailed Statistics

Page 2 Content

`, ]; const pdf = await render({ value: pages, width: 595, // A4 width (pt) height: 842, // A4 height (pt) format: "pdf", mediaType: "print", pdfTitle: "Report 2026", }); await fs.writeFile("report.pdf", Buffer.from(pdf));

Pass HTML templates through pdfHeader / pdfFooter to redraw them on every page. {{pageNumber}} and {{totalPages}} in the template are replaced per page. const pdf = await render({ value: html, format: "pdf", pdfFooter: `
{{pageNumber}} / {{totalPages}}
`, pdfMargin: { top: 24, bottom: 32, left: 24, right: 24 }, }); The footer is normally drawn inside the pdfMargin.bottom band. If the measured footer height exceeds pdfMargin.bottom (including the default 0), the band is widened to the footer height and the content area shrinks by the same amount, which can increase the page count. A footer that fits inside the margin keeps the previous placement and page count.

Instead of writing HTML from scratch, you can use wasm-html-to-image/markdown to automatically build PDFs complete with cover pages, tables of contents, headers, footers, and bookmarks from Markdown. import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image"; import { markdownToDocument } from "wasm-html-to-image/markdown"; const markdown = `--- title: Project Progress Report subtitle: Q4 2026 author: Engineering Directorate date: 2026-10-29 template: report accent: "#1e40af" stamp: CONFIDENTIAL --- # 1. Introduction This report summarises current system migration progress and upcoming milestones. # 2. Status | Milestone | Target Date | Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | Architecture Review | 2026/09/15 | Complete | | PoC Validation | 2026/10/20 | Complete | | Production Rollout | 2026/11/30 | In Progress | # 3. Risk Assessment & Mitigations Details and mitigation strategies are outlined below. `; // markdownToDocument provides the rendered HTML along with PDF metadata & running header/footer const { html, renderOptions } = markdownToDocument(markdown, { paged: true, // Enable page margins and pagination optimization }); const { data: pdfData } = await render({ value: html, format: "pdf", ...renderOptions, }); await fs.writeFile("progress-report.pdf", Buffer.from(pdfData));
documents.s: Generating Professional PDF Reports from Markdown

documents.t: You can generate the same PDF from the command line in a single command: # Basic conversion (auto TOC & bookmarks) npx wasm-html-to-image progress-report.md -o progress-report.pdf # Specify template, accent colour, and stamp npx wasm-html-to-image progress-report.md -o progress-report.pdf --template report --accent "#1e40af" --stamp CONFIDENTIAL

Mass generation of hundreds or thousands of banners using multi-core worker threads. import fs from "node:fs/promises"; import path from "node:path"; import { render } from "wasm-html-to-image/workers"; const items = Array.from({ length: 50 }, (_, i) => ({ id: `card-${i + 1}`, title: `Item #${i + 1}`, })); async function runBatch() { await Promise.all( items.map(async (item) => { const webp = await render({ value: `

${item.title}

`, width: 600, height: 400, format: "webp", }); await fs.writeFile(`./dist/${item.id}.webp`, Buffer.from(webp)); }), ); } runBatch();
Guide to repository setup, build scripts, test suites, and documentation previewing.
pnpm install
# Build html-to-image package pnpm --filter wasm-html-to-image build # Build all monorepo packages pnpm build:js

Requires CMake and Emscripten SDK: cmake -B build -S . -DCMAKE_TOOLCHAIN_FILE=$EMSDK/upstream/emscripten/cmake/Modules/Platform/Emscripten.cmake cmake --build build --target html-to-image Building with the pnpm scripts​ Usually you use these scripts. The output is packages/html-to-image/dist/html-to-image.wasm. pnpm wasm:build # release build (with ThinLTO; this is what you ship) pnpm wasm:build:dev # development build (no ThinLTO) The development build leaves out only link-time optimisation (ThinLTO), so relinking after a one-line C++ change takes seconds instead of minutes. The optimisation level stays at -O3 (lowering it, for example to -O1, breaks the embind glue). The binary is larger and a little slower. Both builds write to the same place, so always rebuild with pnpm wasm:build before you publish. The flags are set again on every run, so switching between the two does not rebuild more than it has to. After rebuilding the WASM, rebuild the package that embeds it. If you do not, the JS and the WASM no longer match: the browser fails at run time, or a new option has no effect. pnpm wasm:build:dev pnpm --filter wasm-html-to-image build # embed the WASM in the package again Native (host) tests​ The Mermaid engine (src/cpp/mermaid) is written with the standard library only, so the unit tests and the compatibility corpus run with the host compiler, without building the WASM. cmake --build build-host-tests --config Debug --target test_mermaid mermaid_cli ./build-host-tests/Debug/test_mermaid.exe # unit tests python tests/mermaid-corpus/run.py # 110 examples taken from the official documentation (exit status 1 on a new failure) mermaid_cli reads a diagram from standard input and writes the SVG. tests/mermaid-corpus/known-gaps.json lists the notations that are not supported yet. When you fix one, remove it from the list too (a fixed entry left in the list fails the run). About timings​ Times from the development build are longer than from the release build. When you record a timing (for example, how long a large flowchart takes to lay out), say which build you measured with.
pnpm --filter wasm-html-to-image test
pnpm --filter visual-test test
# Start local development server with live reload pnpm docs:dev # Build static documentation files pnpm docs:build # Preview built production site pnpm --filter wasm-html-to-image-docs serve
